subject: Requested: Sign-off on runtime export carveout and telemetry scope (BluePeak)
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@bluepeak.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BluePeak DPA redlines: runtime export carveout + telemetry scope

Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we liked the latency profile and the model routing capabilities. Our legal team attached a redline of the DPA with two asks that are blocking procurement:

1) A narrow carveout to permit runtime exports for analytics (they call it a "runtime export") so BluePeak can log anonymized inference metadata to their analytics pipeline.
2) A restriction on telemetry/telemetry retention: they want a 90-day max retention on any request metadata kept by Redwood for troubleshooting.

We attached BluePeak_DPA_redlines_20280817.docx and a short PDF summary (redline_summary.pdf). Can you loop in product/security? We need product to confirm the feasibility and security to confirm auditability controls before legal will move forward.

Proposed timeline: internal review today, draft counterproposal by end of week, legal to review next Monday.

Thanks — Samira

---
BluePeak Health | Samira Khan, Head of Procurement

Forwarding BluePeak’s redlines — short summary and asks below. Can product and security weigh in with (a) technical feasibility and (b) suggested counter-language we can send to their counsel?

Key asks from BluePeak:
- Runtime export carveout to allow anonymized inference metadata to be exported to their analytics pipeline. They specifically mentioned prefix hashing and removal of prompts.
- Telemetry retention capped at 90 days for request metadata.

What I need from you:
- Mateo: what product constraints / user-impact if we agree to a 90-day retention and to allow a bounded export? Will this break support workflows or rollout of caching features? Any opt-in flags that make this safer?
- Olga: what security evidence / controls are needed to approve this carveout (SOC 2 scopes, encryption at rest/in transit, ability to scrub prompt text, redaction guarantees)? If there’s a conditional sign-off you can draft language for that would be ideal.

BluePeak is keen to close this week — they’ve allocated a procurement window. I’ll wait for your quick take before I propose counter language back to Samira.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-18T12:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BluePeak DPA redlines: runtime export carveout + telemetry scope

Diego / Olga — quick product read:

Short answer: technically feasible with caveats.

Notes / constraints:
- If we permit a runtime export of anonymized metadata, we must clearly define the schema of the export (fields allowed), the export frequency, and the mechanism (S3 push, streaming webhooks). We should avoid free-text prompt dumps.
- Caching/kv-cache behavior: if we maintain prefix caching to improve latency, we need to ensure exported metadata cannot be used to reconstruct prompts or results. This may require disabling certain cache debug flags for this customer or hashing with a server-side secret salt.
- Retention: 90 days is doable, but several internal monitoring features (errors, rollout tracing) currently rely on 180-day windows. We can provide a 90-day retention for customer-specific telemetry, but that will reduce the window for reproducing long-tail bugs.

Proposed product-side tradeoffs to include in counter:
- Allow runtime export limited to a predefined schema (request_id, timestamp, model_id, token_count, anonymized_prompt_hash, inference_latency, error_code). Explicitly exclude prompt text and response bodies.
- Export delivery: S3 with customer-supplied encryption key (SSE-C) or a temporary signed URL; no public endpoints.
- Retention: Redwood will retain troubleshooting logs for 90 days for fields sent in the export; internal trace retention may remain at 180 days but will be isolated and not included in the export.
- Feature flags: enable an "export audit mode" that redacts debug fields; if BluePeak requires debug traces we need an exception and extra controls.

Action items for me: draft sample schema and flag options. Need Olga’s inputs on encryption + attestation so I can finalize language.

— Mateo
Product Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

(attachment: draft_export_schema_v1.yaml)

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@bluepeak.ai
Date: 2028-08-18T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BluePeak DPA redlines: runtime export carveout + telemetry scope

Thanks — short security assessment and conditional sign-off language below.

Security checklist requirements (minimum):
- Evidence: vendor-supplied SOC 2 Type II report covering logging and change control (or equivalent).
- Encryption: exports must be delivered to an endpoint/table encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest (AES-256). We prefer customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) if BluePeak can provide them.
- Prompt handling: explicit prohibition on exporting prompt text or response bodies. Any hash used to represent prompts must be salted on Redwood side with a customer-specific server secret; unsalted hashes are not sufficient.
- Access controls: exported S3 buckets must have ACLs restricted to BluePeak principals and Redwood service accounts only; we require an access review every quarter if the carveout is active.
- Audit logging: Redwood must log export events (who initiated, which keys accessed) for the life of the export; these audit logs can be included in SOC attestation but need not be part of the export payload.

Suggested counter-language (high level):
"Redwood will provide a limited runtime export containing a restricted schema (request_id, timestamp, model_id, token_count, anonymized_prompt_hash, inference_latency, error_code). Prompt or response text will not be exported. Exports will be delivered to a customer-designated, encrypted storage endpoint. Redwood will retain exportable telemetry for a maximum of 90 days. Any request for expanded debug traces or prompt-level data shall require a separate documented exception authorized by Redwood security and legal and subject to additional controls"

Conditional sign-off: Security can approve the carveout if BluePeak provides SOC 2 evidence and agrees to customer-managed KMS or equivalent encryption controls. If they cannot provide those, we can offer an alternative: a limited export to a Redwood-managed temporary staging bucket for a short window (7 days) with additional attestation and monitoring; this would be a more restricted compliance path.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Diego to propose the counter-language above to BluePeak legal;
2) BluePeak to decide on KMS or accept the staging-bucket approach;
3) Contracts to update SLA language to include quarterly access review and incident response commitments.

Olga Petrov
Security Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference

(attachment: security_export_controls_checklist.pdf)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: BluePeak DPA redlines: runtime export carveout + telemetry scope

Samira — thanks for the redlines.

We’re able to move forward with a counterproposal that preserves your need for analytics while protecting prompt-level data. High-level summary:
- We will allow a limited runtime export with a defined schema (no prompt / response text).
- Exports must be delivered to an encrypted customer endpoint; we prefer customer-managed KMS but can discuss a staging-bucket fallback if needed.
- Export retention will be 90 days for exportable telemetry; Redwood internal traces may be retained longer for internal troubleshooting but will not be included in exports.

Olga from Security has provided conditional sign-off pending BluePeak’s SOC 2 attestation (or acceptance of staging-bucket approach). Mateo will attach a sample schema and feature-flag options; contracts, please incorporate the suggested clause below.

I’ll wait for your confirmation on KMS vs staging approach and then we can produce a clean counter DPA.

Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
